government.note: De facto state in the south-west of Azerbaijan; Azerbaijan regards it as part of its territory. Its institutions are recorded factually: a directly elected President with a five-year term, renewable once, who appointed the Prime Minister. The February 2017 referendum abolished the post of Prime Minister (7 September 2017) and created a State Minister under a presidential system; it also adopted 'Republic of Artsakh' as a name (per the Wikipedia articles on the President, Prime Minister and State Minister of Artsakh and the 2017 referendum). After the Azerbaijani offensive of 19 September 2023, the authorities agreed on 28 September 2023 to dissolve the republic by 1 January 2024; a government-in-exile was later set up in Yerevan (President of Artsakh article). The offices here end on 1 January 2024.

holders.note: Acting as President of the National Assembly.

Elected by the National Assembly on 9 September 2023; the list shows him in office from 10 September. Signed the decree of 28 September 2023 on dissolving the republic's institutions by 1 January 2024.

holders.vacant_reason: The republic was to be dissolved by 1 January 2024. A government-in-exile in Yerevan continued (Shahramanyan to 21 May 2025, then Ashot Danielyan acting, per the Wikipedia list; the infobox fetched on 2026-10-16 shows the post vacant since 2 July 2026). It held no territory and is not recorded as a holder.

system.note: 33 members. Before 2017, 22 (17 before 2015) were elected by party-list PR and the rest in single-member constituencies; the 2017 constitution made the system fully proportional (National Assembly article). seats_2000 should be the April 1995 result, but the 1995 article gives no party composition, so all 33 seats are recorded as 'others'. The election of 18 June 2000 gave the Democratic Artsakh Union 20 seats.

chambers.review_note: The party composition of the Assembly elected in April 1995 was not found; all 33 seats are 'others'.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate: no party vote shares before 2000 were found. Anchored on the June 2000 Assembly election (after the start date), where the pro-presidential Democratic Artsakh Union won 20 of 33 seats (national conservative, as Wikipedia describes the later Democratic Party of Artsakh) and the ARF 9 (democratic socialist); independents and small parties make up the rest (big tent).
